Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $36 million class fund, distributed automatically using Brightline's membership and payment records, plus $4.5 million for court-approved attorneys' fees and expenses. Automatic distribution is essential given that every member is identifiable. We do not request clear sailing, and any fees not awarded should augment the class fund rather than revert to Brightline. This provides meaningful relief while resolving substantial exposure and avoiding years of further litigation.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic distribution using existing records is appropriate, and can accept independent judicial review of fees with any unawarded fees augmenting class relief. The proposed amount does not sufficiently account for unresolved certification and merits issues or the delay and expense of continued litigation. Brightline proposes a $25 million class fund plus $3 million in court-approved fees and expenses. The class fund would include notice and distribution costs, and the fee allocation would include all counsel expenses; there would be no additional payments beyond those allocations. This offers substantial, direct relief without requiring members to submit claims.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate agreement on automatic payments, independent fee review, and directing any unawarded fees to the class. Certification and merits risks justify compromise, but $25 million leaves room for materially better relief given the disputed charges and the case's survival of dismissal. We counter at a $32 million class fund plus $4 million for court-approved fees and all counsel expenses. Notice and distribution costs may come from the class fund, provided they are reasonable, documented, and subject to court oversight, with a budget disclosed before final approval. No separate payment beyond these allocations would be required. The entire remaining class fund must benefit class members, without reversion to Brightline.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement and agree that reasonable, documented notice and distribution costs should be subject to court oversight, with a budget disclosed before final approval. We also agree that the remaining class fund should benefit members without reversion. Certification remains unresolved, however, and survival of dismissal does not establish liability or recoverable damages across a nationwide class. Brightline can increase its offer to a $26.5 million class fund plus $3.5 million for court-approved attorneys’ fees and all counsel expenses, for a $30 million all-inclusive settlement. Notice, administration, and distribution costs would be paid solely from the class fund, with no additional payments beyond these allocations. Automatic payments, no clear sailing, and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class remain unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We acknowledge the litigation risks and your increased offer. To narrow the remaining gap, we propose a $30 million class fund plus $3.75 million for court-approved attorneys’ fees and all counsel expenses. This reduces both components of our demand while preserving meaningful direct recovery. We retain the agreed automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class. Reasonable, documented notice, administration, and distribution costs will come solely from the class fund, subject to court oversight and a budget disclosed before final approval. The remaining fund must benefit class members without reversion to Brightline, with no payments required beyond these allocations.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Your further movement is constructive. Brightline can increase its offer to a $27.5 million class fund plus $3.5 million for court-approved attorneys’ fees and all counsel expenses—a $31 million all-inclusive settlement. This provides certain, automatic relief now while accounting for unresolved certification, liability, and damages issues. We retain automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class. Reasonable, documented notice, administration, and distribution costs will come solely from the class fund, subject to court oversight and a budget disclosed before final approval. The remaining class fund will benefit class members without reversion to Brightline, and no payments will be required beyond these allocations.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. To focus the remaining gap on relief for members, we accept your proposed $3.5 million allocation for court-approved attorneys’ fees and all counsel expenses and counter with a $29 million class fund, for a $32.5 million total settlement. All other agreed protections remain: automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fees added to the class fund. Reasonable, documented notice, administration, and distribution costs will come solely from the class fund, subject to court oversight and a budget disclosed before final approval. The remaining fund will benefit class members without reversion to Brightline, with no payments required beyond these allocations. This is a complete counterproposal, not acceptance of the current term sheet.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your agreement on the fee allocation. To bridge the remaining gap, Brightline proposes a $28.25 million class fund plus $3.5 million for court-approved attorneys’ fees and all counsel expenses—a $31.75 million all-inclusive settlement, splitting the difference between our current positions. We retain automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class. Reasonable, documented notice, administration, and distribution costs will come solely from the class fund, subject to court oversight and a budget disclosed before final approval. The remaining fund will benefit class members without reversion to Brightline, with no payments required beyond these allocations. We invite acceptance on that basis.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $28.25 million class fund plus $3.5 million for court-approved attorneys’ fees and all counsel expenses, totaling $31.75 million. Acceptance includes automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and addition of any unawarded fees to the class fund. Reasonable, documented notice, administration, and distribution costs will be paid solely from the class fund, subject to court oversight and a budget disclosed before final approval. The remaining class fund will benefit class members without reversion to Brightline, and no additional payments beyond these allocations are required. This is binding acceptance, subject to court approval of the settlement.

Automatic payments are feasible and avoid unnecessary claims barriers. Fees remain subject to independent court review, with any reduction benefiting the class.

The $33.75 million demand is within authority and has approval-friendly terms, but further bargaining could reduce total outlay. With three rounds remaining after this round, increase our total offer by $1 million while preserving the agreed safeguards and leaving room to close.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
Hargrove Lane LLP, court-appointed interim class counsel, submits this declaration in support of preliminary approval under Rule 23(e). Counsel negotiated directly with defense counsel through multiple rounds of proposals and counterproposals addressing both class relief and attorneys’ fees and expenses. Fees were discussed alongside class relief, not only after agreement on class relief. This statement does not disclose confidential mediation offers or communications.

The resulting binding agreement, subject to court approval, provides a $28,250,000 class fund and a separate $3,500,000 allocation for court-approved attorneys’ fees and all counsel expenses. Payments will be distributed automatically using Brightline’s records, without requiring claim forms. Reasonable, documented notice, administration, and distribution costs will be paid from the class fund, subject to court oversight and a budget disclosed before final approval. The remaining class fund will benefit class members without reversion to Brightline. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any fees the Court declines to award will augment the class fund rather than revert to Brightline.

Counsel believes the settlement is fair, reasonable, and adequate for purposes of preliminary approval. The class fund represents approximately 44.1% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges before administration costs and any addition of unawarded fees. Although the action survived dismissal, class certification remains unresolved, and continued litigation presents substantial certification, liability, and damages risks. Trial would be approximately two to three years away. The settlement provides substantial monetary relief without requiring the class to prevail on those contested issues, while automatic distribution avoids the participation barriers associated with a claims process.

Counsel recognizes that simultaneous negotiation of fees and class relief warrants scrutiny. The absence of clear sailing, independent judicial review of fees, and allocation of unawarded fees to the class are meaningful safeguards, but do not substitute for the Court’s independent evaluation. Counsel requests preliminary approval and authorization of appropriate class notice. Final approval should follow review of the administration budget, proposed allocation and distribution procedures, adequacy of notice, class-member responses, the fee application, and the other requirements of Rule 23(e), including equitable treatment of class members.
